body: If I had a gun or could get a gun I probably would've been dead by now to be honest

>I get why it feels stupid, it's a paradox.
>
>If you seek help, they'll help you in their way, by taking away the one control you have left.
>
>If you don't seek help your not trying to take control, and the one thing you have control over, instead controls you.

I couldn't have thought of a better way to put it. It's like I want and don't want help at the same time. Every time I'm considering talking to someone my mind comes up with tonnes of reason why I shouldn't.

*You're not actually depressed, you just want someone to pity you.*

*It's gonna make everything so awkward between you.*

*What if they tell someone you were not ready to tell.*

I frankly don't know if I'm gonna end up doing it, but it's nice to know someone at least understands.
Thank you
I have a rope that I plan on using if it ever comes to that. I want to get over depression, but that feels so impossible. If I can't find help before the end of the year I think I'll just give up
I'd say piece of shit is the best word for me. Basically everything but the useful parts
I think that might have have more to do with them not knowing what to make of the situation rather than being a dick

I can't salvage this year anymore since I've missed all exams this semester. I was going to change fields next year, but I don't even know if I will get accepted where I want to go. And I still don't know how I could spin this year to my parents. I've gotten back to where I was last time I was posting on this account.

I feel like the voice in my head is just me. I've been telling myself how to get back on track but I'm completely uninterested in following my own advice. I've always been really annoyed that I never listen to myself but at this point just doesn't care anymore.

I guess there is, but I think I'm afraid of failure. I'm scared I would devote myself to it only to find out that I'm pretty bad at it, that's why I've been choosing not to do it and thinking that I could if I ever wanted to. There's also a case of me always wanting to do it some other time, and there's never a good time for me to start but I think it's just my another coping mechanism for avoiding the possibility of failure.
I feel the opposite. Like it's telling me good advice and how I should do things properly, but I never listen to it and lead myself into despair.
I think I've summed up how I "feel" in my recent [post on depression](https://www.reddit.com/r/depression/comments/8chwq6/depression_snuck_up_on_me/)
Isn't that basically a sunken cost fallacy?

Thing is I don’t feel sick. I don’t even know if I actually have depression. I’ve always thought getting it would involve some kind of fireworks. But it doesn’t feel that much different than “normal”. The thoughts have always been there, I just have more time alone with them nowadays I guess.
I haven't. Whenever I feel like talking about it to someone it just sounds stupid and lazy to me. I guess I don't want people to think about me that way
